gloss: beginning; opening; start of an era

definitions.gloss: raising of the curtain; opening of a performance
definitions.explanation: The literal raising of the curtain at the start of a theatrical performance.

definitions.gloss: beginning; start; dawn of a new era
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, the start of something significant such as a new period, movement, or chapter in history.

examples.japanese: {幕開|まくあ}け⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{観客|かんきゃく}→観客：02556_kankyaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{引|ひ}きつける⟦{舞台|ぶたい}→舞台：03606_butai⟧だった。
examples.english: It was a performance that captivated the audience from the opening.

examples.japanese: ⟦{華|はな}やか→華やか：06070_hanayaka⟧な⟦{演出|えんしゅつ}→演出：04460_enshutsu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{幕開|まくあ}け⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}った→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧。
examples.english: The opening was adorned with a spectacular production.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{幕開|まくあ}けだ。
examples.english: It is the dawn of a new era.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{発明|はつめい}→発明：01495_hatsumei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{産業革命|さんぎょうかくめい}→産業革命：18638_sangyoukakumei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{幕開|まくあ}け⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: This invention marked the beginning of the industrial revolution.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{近代化|きんだいか}→近代化：15055_kindaika⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{幕開|まくあ}け⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{明治維新|めいじいしん}→明治維新：16286_meijiishin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧さかのぼる。
examples.english: The dawn of Japan's modernization can be traced back to the Meiji Restoration.

notes:
USAGE:
{幕開|まくあ}け originally refers to the raising of a theater curtain. It is now widely used figuratively to mean the start of a significant new period or era.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {幕開|まくあ}け⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}る→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧ (to mark the opening)
- ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{幕開|まくあ}け (the dawn of a new era)
- {幕開|まくあ}け⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to serve as the beginning)

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{開幕|かいまく}→開幕：08174_kaimaku⟧ also means the start of a performance or event but is more commonly used for sports seasons, festivals, or formal events. {幕開|まくあ}け is preferred for figurative uses describing historical or cultural turning points.
